biography:
Walter Röhrl, a name whispered with a mix of awe and trepidation in the German touring car scene, burst onto the racing stage with the subtlety of a V8 engine screaming to life. Hailing from Regensburg, his early years were less about karting championships and more about tearing through the Bavarian countryside in his father's Opel Kadett, much to the chagrin of the local constabulary. It was during one of these impromptu 'time trials' that a local racer, impressed by Röhrl's raw talent (and perhaps scared by his reckless abandon), suggested he try his hand at a proper race. Röhrl entered a local hill climb, borrowed a friend's souped-up VW Beetle, and promptly shattered the course record. 

That single victory ignited a fire within him. He sold his beloved motorcycle, scraped together enough money to enter a DTM feeder series, and quickly proved his mettle. The aggressive style that had irked his father now thrilled fans and intimidated rivals. In the Audi V8 quattro DTM team, he's a rising star, pushing the limits of both man and machine, earning a reputation for daring overtakes and nail-biting finishes. 

However, some question whether his impetuous nature will lead to future problems, or if he will learn to use strategy and control. The Audi team has taken a bet on his talent, and Walter is determined to prove them right. He is currently working with a dedicated pit crew and coach to hone his talent. 

Now at just 21 years of age, his career is taking off, and he is poised to make an impact on the sport.
drivingStyle: Röhrl's driving style is a visceral blend of aggression and precision. He attacks corners with a ferocity that borders on reckless, often throwing the car into a slide and relying on his lightning-fast reflexes to maintain control. He favors late braking and isn't afraid to use every inch of the track, often venturing onto the kerbs and even the grass in pursuit of speed. While his tire management could use improvement, his ability to handle pressure is remarkable; he thrives in high-stakes situations, often pulling off daring overtakes in the closing laps of a race.

rivalries.reason: A veteran DTM driver, Richter publicly criticized Röhrl's driving style as 'dangerous' and 'unprofessional' after a near-collision at the Norisring. This has led to fierce on-track battles and heated exchanges in the media.

Klein, another young up-and-comer, consistently out-qualifies Röhrl, forcing him to fight his way through the pack. Röhrl sees her as a direct threat to his ambitions and is determined to prove his superiority on the track.
Marco Lorenz, an experienced driver who also comes from Röhrl's hometown, sees him as an upstart. Both drivers compete for the same sponsors, creating tension both on and off the track.

quirks: Always wears a lucky charm (a small wooden carving of a Bavarian lion) inside his racing suit.
Refuses to speak to anyone for 30 minutes before a race, preferring to listen to heavy metal music on noise-canceling headphones.
Insists on having a specific type of apple strudel (made by his grandmother) in the pit garage before every race.
famousQuote: You have to attack like there's no tomorrow, because in racing, there often isn't.
careerHighlight: Winning the Hockenheimring DTM race in his rookie season, overtaking two championship contenders in the final lap to secure his first victory.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the Nürburgring after misjudging a corner in wet conditions, costing him valuable championship points.
